articleTitle: The Characters Interaction Design Framework of Preschool Children’s Educational Games
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: With the development of the times, educational games, as the tool distinct from traditional teaching methods, have gradually become a necessity for preschool families. Based on preschool children’s developmental characteristics, this paper integrates cognitive schema theory, observations of children’s spontaneous play and successful design cases. It argues that the core of educational game design lies in characters interaction design. A refined design framework is presented, and the viewpoint is validated through practice. The results show that the quality of character interaction design in educational games significantly impacts children’s acceptance. Positive character interaction enhances gameplay experience, promotes active learning, encourages repeated engagement, and effectively constructs their Zone of Proximal Development.

articleTitle: GPNN:Grouped Point-NN for more efficient point cloud classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Point cloud is irregular and permutation-invariant, unlike grid-based data such as images, posing unique challenges for effective analysis and processing. PointNN, proposed by Zhang et al., introduces a non-parametric network for point cloud analysis, achieving competitive performance on multiple 3D tasks without any learnable parameters or training. However, the pooling operation in the model can lead to a sharp reduction in the number of features, resulting in a considerable loss of important information. To solve this issue, we introduce an enhancement mechanism termed "Subset Division(SD)" into the original PointNN. "Subset Division" is a simple mechanism where the input point cloud is divided into multiple subsets before being fed into the model. Despite the simple mechanism of "Subset Division" can enhance classification performance, and "PointNN+SD" achieves a higher classification performance of 82.2% on ModelNet40 compared to the original PointNN. PointPN adds a few learnable linear layers to the base model PointNN and improves its classification accuracy by incorporating "subset division." Additionally, by ensembling the output results of "PointNN+SD" and the original, we achieve an even greater classification accuracy of 83.7%, higher than either model individually.

articleTitle: An Enabling Architecture for Computational Cost Efficiency in Predictive Maintenance Digital Twins
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: As digital twins emerge to provide a replication of physical assets in the digital space, the application of predictive maintenance of industrial asset becomes more effective. Developing digital twins for the predictive maintenance case study leverages Internet of Things, cloud computing and machine learning. While these technologies extend the necessary tools for deploying predictive maintenance digital twins, an enabling architecture facilitated by fog computing positions predictive maintenance digital twins for improved computational cost and latency than centralizing in the cloud or running locally at the edge. This work presents the application of a distributed digital framework, showing the benefits of better compute utilization and latency by adopting a distributed digital twin framework for predictive maintenance of wind turbine components in a wind farm.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerant Trajectory Tracking Control for Underactuated UUV based on Fast Terminal Sliding Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: We address the trajectory tracking problem for underactuated unmanned underwater vehicle(UUV) in the presence of actuator failure. Firstly, we reconstruct the UUV model according to the possible actuator failures in practice. Then, the third-order sliding mode passive fault tolerant controller was designed. And we prove the controller satisfy the Lyapunov stability. Finally, we demonstrate the controller can complete the established control tasks and has good performance under limited fault conditions through numerical simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Research on Velocity-Coordinated Leader-Follower Cooperative Path Following Control Method for UUV Formations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a leader-follower cooperative path following control mechanism for Unmanned Underwater Vehicle (UUV) formations to address the challenge of coordinated path following. By tackling the relatively independent problems of path following control and formation coordination control, the mechanism enables multiple UUVs to maintain formation while accurately following the desired path. First, a guidance law was developed for the path following control of underactuated UUVs by extending the Line-of-Sight (LOS) method, and a controller was designed using sliding mode control and backstepping techniques to allow both leaders and followers to track the desired path. Second, a velocity-coordinated formation control method was employed to achieve cooperative path following while minimizing communication overhead. Third, to address communication delay issues, a delay compensation method based on position estimation was designed, which reduces the desired position error of followers during the formation coordination process. Finally, simulation experiments were conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The Simulation Design of Attitude Control of Cruise Missile Based on Fireworks Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Attitude control of cruise missiles is a key technology for flight stability and accuracy. This paper establishes an attitude dynamics model and analyzes the attitude changes of cruise missiles during flight. It compares attitude calculation methods using algorithms such as the fourth-order Runge-Kutta, improved Euler method, and second-order Runge-Kutta. The convergence of accuracy is tested using the Fireworks Algorithm, and a dynamic model is established through Simulink simulation to test and analyze long-term stable flight by adjusting time and control parameters. The research results provide new ideas and methods for the attitude control of cruise missiles, with significant theoretical and practical implications. With continuous technological advancements, cruise missiles will play an increasingly important role in both military and civilian fields in the future.

articleTitle: PCB Defect Detection Method Based on G-YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: In the electronics industry, PCB is crucial for ensuring the product quality. However, these defects of PCB generally have the characteristics of complex backgrounds, small sizes and similar features, resulting in the issues of high computational complexity or low detection precision of PCB defect detection algorithms based on deep learning. To resolve the aforementioned concerns, this paper proposed a lightweight PCB defect detection model named G-YOLOv8 which was based on the YOLOv8. The G-YOLOv8 can effectively reduce the computational complexity by integrating the Ghost Conv into the Backbone and Neck networks. Furthermore, the G-C2f module was introduced into Neck network to strengthen the capability of G-YOLOv8 to perceive the feature information at different scales and semantic levels, thus improving the detection performance of the model for the PCB defect. Meanwhile, the performance of G-YOLOv8 model was evaluated on the public data set. The experimental results show that the parameter number of G-YOLOv8 is 2.6 million, which is decreased by 89.7% and 13.3% compared with SSD and YOLOv8, respectively. The computational load of G-YOLOv8 is 7.5 GFLOPs, which is decreased by 93.5% and 7.4% compared with SSD and YOLOv8, respectively. The mAP@0.5 of G-YOLOv8 is 94.4%, which is increased by 4.8% and 1.3% compared with SSD and YOLOv8, respectively. Hence, in the task of PCB defect detection, the G-YOLOv8 model can reduce the computational complexity while preserving a high detection precision, which can meet the requirements of PCB defect detection in industrial scenarios.

articleTitle: Architecture of Advanced Onboard Equipment Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: An architecture for the advanced onboard equipment control system and the architecture of its constituent components is proposed, utilizing the concept of distributed integrated modular avionics. The system performs aircraft system functions with a designated design assurance level of "A". This approach allows for a reduction in the aircraft's cabling weight, enhances the electromagnetic interference protection of transmitted information, and increases the overall reliability of the system.

articleTitle: Quick Deployment Control System for Small Police Unmanned Boat
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: In recent years, with increasing global investment in Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) research, there has been rapid development in the technology of small police USVs. However, there are still some delays in the design of rapid deployment for small police USVs. Traditional deployment methods, such as tower crane and swing arm types, are complex in operation, slow in deployment speed, and have limited safety and wave resistance. This paper proposes a design scheme for a rapid deployment control system for small police USVs, using a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) as the control core. The system integrates slide rail modules, hydraulic modules, and laser rangefinder modules to achieve rapid deployment functionality. Simulation experiments validate the feasibility of this new rapid deployment system scheme and demonstrate that it improves deployment efficiency while simultaneously enhancing safety and wave resistance capabilities.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Dynamic Dual-Channel Supply Chain with Sales Efforts
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The dynamic decision in a multi-stage dual-channel supply chain involving one manufacturer and one retailer is carried out in this paper. Stackelberg game models dominated by manufacturer under decentralized and centralized scenarios are established. Backward induction is applied to derive the optimal solutions, based on which exploring the influence of previous-stage pricing on pricing, sales efforts and profit of current stage. The comparison between the proposed multi-stage pricing model and conventional constant pricing model is conducted to demonstrate that multi-stage dynamic pricing contributes to promoting profits. Besides, supply chain system without sales effort is also studied to verify the necessity of considering sales efforts into supply chain management for manufacturer and retailer. Finally, sensitivity analysis and numerical simulations are carried out to confirm the obtained results.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Optimal Path Planning Algorithms Using Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: In this paper effective algorithms of optimal route planning in the presence of threat zones and uncertainties with the use of deep learning technology are considered. At the present time, in theory, there are a huge number of algorithms to determine the shortest route, which are widely used to create optimal aircrafts pathways in order to achieve their required destination. A comparative analysis of two investigated methods is carried out: A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> (A-star) and Dijkstra’s algorithm. The discussed algorithms are compared according to two criteria: the length of the shortest trajectory found and searching steps count. The analytical and graphical results of the comparison are presented. Because of the artificial intellect development, there are many possibilities for applying deep learning methods to build optimal path planning algorithms and methodology in the future. Conclusions about considered methods advantages and their application field have been made according to the performed estimation.

articleTitle: Global and Local Fusion Method for Path Planning and Formation Control of Multiple Unmanned Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: This paper studies a formation path planning controller for multiple unmanned systems (MUS) based on the leader-follower structure. We proposed a combination of global and local planning algorithm and designed the algorithm details for the leader and the follower respectively. The leader was designed to complete path planning task by using a hybrid planning method. Specifically, we chose the jump point search (JPS) algorithm removing some redundant outputs as the global path-finding algorithm, and the deep Q network (DQN) algorithm as the local algorithm. For the follower, the DQN algorithm is adopted to keep appropriate distances with the leader. And the details of the DQN algorithm are designed separately. Finally, we conducted experiments in the Gazebo simulation environment The results show that the framework is executable and robust and it can enable MUS to avoid collisions and achieve the end point

articleTitle: Research on Informative Path Planning Using Deep Reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Efficient data gathering is important for mapping and surveilling for many applications on the Earth's surface. In large-area monitoring situations, executing a crew of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) provides enhanced spatial coverage and reliability against individual malfunctions. Yet, a major obstacle is developing cooperative path-planning strategies that allow UAVs to accomplish a collaborative mission objective. We present a new Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-based (MARL) informative path planning approach for adjustable landscape surveilling using UAV crews. Our approach presents innovative network representations facilitating effective path planning in 3D workspaces. By utilizing a counterfactual baseline, our method effectively resolves the problem of credit assignment to learn cooperative behavior. Our findings demonstrate that enhanced planning performance. Experimental results show that our method outclasses other non-learning-based techniques while generalizing well to various team sizes and communication scenarios.

articleTitle: Yolo-EV2: An Industrial Mining Conveyor Belt Tear Detection Model Based on Improved Yolov5 Algorithm for Efficient Backbone Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Real-time detection of conveyor belt tearing is of great significance to ensure mining in the coal industry. The longitudinal tear damage problem of conveyor belts has the characteristics of multi-scale, abundant small targets, and complex interference sources. To address these characteristics, we propose a visual detection method Yolo-EV2 based on deep learning. Firstly, a multi-case conveyor belt tear datasets is developed for complex interference and small-size detection. Secondly, the conveyor belt tear detection method Yolo-EV2 is designed, which utilizes the EfficientNetV2 to improve the network Backbone, so as to enhance the feature fusion ability of the model for small tear targets and reduce the computational volume of the overall detection model. A large number of compartment experiments with existing target detection networks on conveyor belt tear detection show that Yolo-EV2 has a better performance in both Map value and FPS, which can meet the demand of real-time detection and is expected to be used in industrial practice.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Guidance for 3D Driver Pose Estimation with Diffusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Recognition of driver behavior in autonomous driving environments not only captures risky behaviors such as driver distraction in a timely manner, but also has great potential to improve human-vehicle communication and increase personalized comfort in driving. Diffusion modeling has revolutionized several application areas, but 3D pose estimation for drivers is still involved. In this paper, we propose a novel 3D driver action estimation method, named DiffDrive, which achieves more robust and accurate pose estimation in driving environments in the face of dark light and occlusion by effectively incorporating a multi-modal conditional prior in the diffusion process to guide the global structures. We evaluate the effectiveness of DiffDrive and its superiority over existing models using the Drive&Act dataset.

articleTitle: VDFSR Knowledge based Variable-Density Photographic Film to Sound Generation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Image domain film to sound generation (IDFSG) is a research hotspot in film industry and cross-modal learning. Existing researches neglect sound generation need for variable density film soundtrack. To solve the problem of constructing sound generation processes during variable density film soundtrack reproduction (VDFSR), we propose a PF2SG method based on the VDFSR knowledge, which can effectively achieve high-quality sound generation performance. Specifically, from the perspective of mining the intrinsic consistency of different types of signal capability transformations, we embed variable density film soundtrack reproduction knowledge into the corresponding sound generation process in stages. Moreover, to further enhance the stability of our IDFSG method, we design a sound reproduction module for variable density film soundtrack that integrates the photometric sampling interval based on the mechanical structure of the film projector. Our method effectively explores the intrinsic consistency between the image domain information and the audio domain information during VD film sound generation. Experiments have shown that our method can effectively generate higher quality audio compared to existing methods and commercial devices.

articleTitle: Static Deadlock Detection for Interrupt-driven Embedded Software
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Interrupt-driven embedded software is widely used in safety-critical systems, where any occurrence of errors can lead to serious consequences. Deadlock is a common concurrency error, and deadlock detection methods are mainly designed for multi-threaded programs. However, due to the differences in concurrency control and preemption mechanisms between interrupt-driven programs and multi-threaded programs, the existing deadlock detection methods for multi-threaded programs cannot be directly applied to interrupt-driven programs. A static deadlock detection method is proposed for interrupt-driven programs to enhance the reliability and safety of interrupt-driven embedded software. Building upon the traditional context-sensitive lockset analysis, this method takes into account the concurrent semantics of interrupts and extends the lock graph model. Our method effectively reduces false positives by analyzing the concurrent relationships of cycles in a lock graph. Based on these methods, we develop a deadlock detection tool, and experiments are conducted with it. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively detect deadlocks related to interrupts.

articleTitle: A Channel Fusion Convolutional Neural Network for Lung Nodule Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The automatic and precise detection of lung nodules in 3D Computed Tomography (CT) scans is essential for effective lung cancer screening. However, most current methods process CT images slice-by-slice, overlooking inter-slice information. Exploring the inter-slice correlation of 3D CT images is a potential way to enhance the effectiveness of lung nodule detection even further. To deal with this issue, we design a Channel Fusion Convolutional Neural Network (CFCNNet) aimed at detecting pulmonary nodules. Notably, we design a Group Shuffle module (GS module) to fuse the inter-slice feature, which enhances the discrimination and extraction of corresponding information for nodules of varying sizes within the same set of slices. Our ablation study and experimental results on the publicly accessible LUNA16 dataset indicate that the suggested approach significantly improves detection sensitivity, the Competition Performance Metric (CPM) score reaches 89.69%, outperforms other contemporary detection methods.

articleTitle: An Improved Algorithm for Spiking Neural Networks with Multi-Scale Attention Coding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), driven by spike-based mechanisms, are known for their high efficiency and low energy consumption, which makes them ideal for applications like image classification, object detection, and medical diagnostics. However, challenges include training difficulties due to the non-differentiability of spiking activities and limitations in encoding schemes, which struggle to capture complex spatio-temporal dynamics. In this paper, we propose a novel algorithm, termed the Spatio-Temporal Backpropagation algorithm with Multi-Scale Attention Coding (STBP-MSC). STBP-MSC dynamically allocates attention across spatial and temporal domains, which improves coding efficiency and enhances the classification accuracy of SNNs. Furthermore, STBP-MSC incorporates the Complementary Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (CLIF) neuron model, which enhances temporal gradient computation. Experimental results on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets demonstrate that STBP-MSC achieves high coding efficiency and superior performance within minimal time windows.

articleTitle: Survey of Malware Detection through Use of Neural Network Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: In general, antivirus software has heavily relied on signature-based detection methods. These antivirus products usually reference a database of known malicious signatures, making them naturally susceptible to previously unseen malware samples. One of the easiest ways for malware authors to produce these new malware samples is by applying various obfuscation techniques to the previously existing malware. This paper will survey a newer approach to malware detection through neural networks by gathering results from recent journal articles and conference papers published in various online databases. These artificial intelligence-oriented solutions show promise in resilience to unfamiliar malware variants. Explicitly focusing on obfuscated malware, it will compare detection rates between signature-based and neural network-based malware detection systems and organize results using various NN models and training features. Overall, the survey finds that signature-based methods detect between 50 and 80 percent of obfuscated malware samples, while all but one of the neural network methods detect between 90 and 99 percent. This considerable increase in performance suggests that neural networks might provide an effective alternate or supplemental detection method for antivirus products.

articleTitle: An attention-based dual-evaluation learning architecture for collaborative target encirclement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: For multi-agent collaborative encirclement tasks, this paper addresses the challenges encountered in traditional multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) methods, particularly the constraints posed by credit assignment and low learning efficiency issues. To tackle these problems, a modified MADRL algorithm is developed specifically for multi-agent systems, integrating a dual critic network and a multi-head attention mechanism. The dual critic network comprises a local critic network and a global critic network, with each network independently assessing the effectiveness of actions for the individual agent and the team, respectively, to achieve a balanced benefit. The multi-head attention mechanism is incorporated into the global critic network, and the attention weight of each agent is dynamically allocated to ensure that key information is effectively and precisely captured and processed, thereby alleviating the influence of local features and biases, and addressing the issue of low learning efficiency. A segmented reward function is designed to analyze the advantages and disadvantages of agent actions by calculating the distance between each agent and the escape target, and then comprehensively evaluating the behavioral value of all agents, so as to promote cooperative behavior. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed system yields substantial improvements in performance metrics, including encirclement speed, travel distance, and encirclement success rate.

articleTitle: Group Recommendation Method Based on Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Group activities are becoming more and more common on the Internet in the big data environment. Which makes many scholars focus on how to recommend items or activities to a group. However, conventional recommendation systems grapple with issues like data sparsity and the cold start problem, which limits the relevance and accuracy of recommendation. Therefore, this paper conducts an in-depth exploration of group recommendation methods utilizing graph neural networks and introduces a novel recommendation framework aimed at enhancing the efficacy of group recommendations. Firstly, this paper discusses how to construct an effective graph structure to encode the social interaction and individual characteristics of users. Then, an improved graph neural network architecture is proposed. Finally, extensive experimental evaluation is carried out on actual datasets, and the findings demonstrate that our framework markedly enhances the accuracy of recommendations.

articleTitle: IoT-based Leftover Food Segmentation System for Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Due to declining birthrate and aging population in our society, the number of people in need of care is increasing. Recording the amount of leftover food by care recipients is a critical task; However, due to the shortage of caregivers, automation through IoT-based system is required. This paper proposes a user-friendly leftover detection system using Android device to reducing caregiver burden and improving the accuracy of leftover measurements for monitoring health. This system includes functionalities for easy annotation, training, and inference execution on Android. Additionally, the system is designed to allow the selection of continuous learning as a training method, enabling the model to be trained with newly added data in a short amount of time. The AI model used in this system not only infers leftover areas from input images but also implements algorithms for detecting anomalous inputs. In the experiments, the our system’s inference performance for leftover rice and soup achieved a mIoU of 0.876. And the implementation of continuous learning significantly reduced training time while maintaining model performance, enhancing system efficiency and user-friendliness. In anomaly detection, the system was able to effectively exclude data unrelated to the meal setup. Future work includes incorporating advanced AI models, such as SAM, to assist the annotation process, further alleviating user burden.

articleTitle: Color Image Segmentation of Dental Caries Using U-Net Enhanced with Residual Blocks and Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The rapid progress of artificial intelligence and deep learning has greatly influenced several areas, particularly in healthcare, with computer vision displaying outstanding capabilities in diagnosing and treating patients. Using image analysis in dentistry shows great potential for improving oral healthcare through the identification of dental conditions. The goal of this research is to identify dental calculus and cavities by separating color images into two classes using various U-Net model designs. Three U-Net models are suggested: one with a VGG16 backbone, another with attention gates to highlight important features, and a third combining residual blocks with attention gates. The research made use of a collection of RGB images taken by a dental expert with an intraoral camera within a six-month period. The outcomes show that advanced U-Net structures perform exceptionally well in segmenting dental problems from color images, with the attention residual U-Net achieving a top training accuracy of 84.8%. This study highlights the possibility of creating mobile dental care systems that provide convenient, customized, and effective oral healthcare services.

articleTitle: Oracle Primitive Topology Segmentation Algorithm Based on Mask R-CNN and U-net deep Learning Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: In this paper, considering that the topology is irregular and the data set is small, histogram equalization is used to enhance image contrast, which is conducive to identifying the target boundary, Gaussian blur is used to smooth the image, and image rotation is used to enhance the data. Finally, Sobel operator is used to extract image features from horizontal and vertical directions, and non-local mean method and bilateral filtering are used to discriminate and deal with the identified interference factors. According to the characteristics of the data set and the irregular features of the single word, the data set was normalized and masked by segmentation. The improved Region-based CNN algorithm Mask R-CNN algorithm was used to identify and segment the image, and the single word recognition model was established to make it have good local perception and be able to identify the local features in the image. At the same time, in order to reduce the fitting risk and comprehensively evaluate the model, ten-fold cross-validation is used to improve the training effect of the model. Then, image feature extraction, noise reduction and pixel normalization are carried out on the original topology image, and Ada optimization is carried out on the established single word recognition model to accelerate the convergence of the Mask R-CNN model. Combined with the newly established U-Net model, 200 preprocessed oracle rubbings are trained and segmented.

articleTitle: An Improved Algorithm for Flight Maneuver Recognition and Evaluation Based on Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The advancement of defense capabilities relies heavily on improving air combat proficiency. Effective pilot training plays a pivotal role in achieving this goal. Simulated flight training is a critical method for training pilots, and leveraging intelligent scoring algorithms can significantly enhance pilot proficiency. In this study, we propose an enhanced SVM algorithm that incorporates PCA for dimensionality reduction. By combining pilot training-related data from flight simulators with advanced machine learning techniques, we aim to develop an intelligent digital instructor system. This system provides real-time, objective, and quantitative assessments, along with detailed diagnostic feedback to pilot trainees. Furthermore, the algorithm’s potential extends beyond civilian pilot training to autonomous air combat scenarios involving UCAVs in the future.

articleTitle: Decentralized Multi-robot Path Planning using Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Communication plays a key role for fruitful decentralized multi-robot path planning. However, it is quite difficult to discern which insight is necessary to perform the assignment, when and how it should be exchanged among robots. To avoid these problems and go beyond the ad hoc design of heuristics, we introduce an integrated model that generates coherent, inter-communication and decision-making for robots operating in a confined working environment. The architecture of our work includes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to achieve sufficient patterns from nearby sensing and a graph neural network (GNN) to share these characteristics within robots. This trained network mimics an expert algorithm and can be employed online in decentralized planning where we have only local interaction and observations. In the simulation-based evaluation, we steer group of robots to their goals in 2D complex work environments. We compute the success probability and total cost along each of planned strategies. The performance of our algorithm is nearly the same as our expert algorithm, which proves the potency of the advocated technique. Specifically, we demonstrate that our model allows for testing on new cases (large environments, a larger number of robots).

articleTitle: Multi-Strategy Hybrid Grey Wolf Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: This paper presents an improved Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) algorithm that incorporates multiple strategies to enhance both convergence speed and solution accuracy. These strategies include the integration of a backward learning approach during the population initialization phase, the implementation of a dynamic adjustment mechanism for adaptive factors, the employment of a multi-population strategy to increase population diversity, and the introduction of a local search mechanism to improve solution precision. The efficacy of the proposed algorithm was validated through simulations conducted on ten standard test functions, which demonstrated significant improvements in convergence speed, stability, and global search capability.

articleTitle: Improved Dingo Optimization Algorithm for Human-robot Collaborative U-shaped Disassembly Line Balancing Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: There is increasing attention on remanufacturing, with the primary focus in the industry on recovering reusable products to generate profit. In the process of optimizing remanufacturing, addressing the balance issue in the operation of the disassembly line is crucial. Therefore, this study proposes the use of an improved Dingo Optimization Algorithm (IDOA) and designs a mathematical model for human-robot collaboration to explore how to achieve higher profits under these conditions. Finally, the improved IDOA is experimentally compared with the commercial optimization solver CPLEX and another intelligent optimization method—the Battle Royale Optimization (BRO). The results demonstrate that this method offers high quality and efficiency.

articleTitle: Acoustic Simultaneous Localization and Mapping for Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The current technology employed for autonomous driving has provided us with satisfactory performance and results. However, some of the most commonly used sensors, such as LiDAR and cameras, are typically high-priced and often require tremendous amount of computational power to process the collected data. In many cases, the adverse weather and night-time conditions hinder the performance of vision-based sensors. In this paper, we propose an alternative approach for enhancing the current sensing methodologies by utilizing acoustic signatures of moving objects. This approach makes use of a microphone array to collect and process acoustic signatures captured for simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Rather than using numerous sensors to gather information of the surrounding environment of the ego vehicle, this method investigates the benefits of considering the sound waves of different objects around the ego vehicle and offers a cost-effective approach for SLAM.

articleTitle: Research on Maximum Power Point Tracking Control Based on Wind Power Generation Control System of Marine Ranch
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: In this paper, a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) simulation experiment is conducted using an H-type vertical axis wind turbine as the experimental control object. First, the mathematical model of the controlled object is established. Based on this model, an aerodynamic torque observer is designed to assess external disturbances, and a backstepping control strategy for MPPT is developed and tested. The simulation results show that, compared to traditional backstepping control, the improved backstepping control algorithm reduces adjustment time by 37% and overshoot by 50%. These findings demonstrate that the improved backstepping control algorithm offers superior control performance.

articleTitle: Dust Weather Image Clarity Algorithm Based on Color Adjustment and Dark Channel Dehazing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: To solve the problem of color deviation and low contrast in dust weather images, a image clarity algorithm based on color adjustment and dark channel fogging is proposed from the perspective of image restoration. The improved Gaussian model is first used in the proposed algorithm to correct and stretch the RGB three channels, solving the problem of image color deviation. On this basis, the pixel level atmospheric light value map is calculated based on the light and dark channel data, and the transmittance of the sky and prospective areas is modified by a threshold, which is obtained based on the statistical characteristics of those areas, sloving the distortion problem of the sky and prospective areas in the restored image. Finally, the overall brightness of the restored image is optimized by iteratively adjusting the atmospheric light value. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively solve the distortion problem of the sky and prospective areas, ensure the appropriate brightness, enhance the image contrast, and restore the real color of the image scene.

articleTitle: Dynamic Guidance Point Obstacle Avoidance Planning Method and Optimization Based on DWA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Currently, global-local two-layer path planning is usually adopted when robots perform area coverage cleaning tasks in unfamiliar environments. However, due to the limited detection range of the sensors carried by the robot, when the robot encounters unknown obstacles during the planning of local paths, the robot is prone to deviate from the original planned route during obstacle avoidance, resulting in a decrease in the coverage rate of the cleaning task. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a dynamic guided point obstacle avoidance method based on the Dynamic Window Approach (DWA). The method is that when the robot performs the cleaning task, through constantly updating the perception information and environmental data, the system dynamically selects the guide point on the global path as the temporary target point, and then constantly adjusts the driving direction and speed to ensure that the robot can return to the preset global path while avoiding obstacles. In addition, the evaluation function is improved for this application scenario. This enables the robot to safely and smoothly avoid obstacles when operating autonomously in unfamiliar environments, navigate and travel autonomously in the global path, and improve cleaning task coverage.

articleTitle: Energy-saving path planning method for unmanned surface vehicles based on curiosity-driven reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Reasonable global path planning techniques for unmanned surface vehicles (USV) can improve work efficiency. A global path planning method based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed to reduce the energy consumption of USVs in environments with current. Firstly, a simulation experimental environment is built based on electronic charts (EC) and current models to simulate the real environment. Then, the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) training framework based on the intrinsic curiosity module (ICM) is built to enhance the exploration ability and improve the training efficiency. Subsequently, an external reward strategy is designed based on reward reshaping policy to suppress excessive random exploration of curiosity. Finally, simulation and comparative experiments are conducted to verify the algorithm's effectiveness.

articleTitle: An Infrared-Visible Image Fusion Network with Multi-Scale Convolutional Attention and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF) obtains an information-rich fused image by fusing the intensity information in infrared images and the texture information in visible light images. However, existing methods usually have difficulty in effectively balancing global and edge feature extraction while maintaining cross-modal consistency, resulting in unsatisfactory fusion quality. In this paper, a cross-modal multi-scale dual-branch feature fusion network named MTFuse is proposed to address the key challenges of IVIF, including global and edge feature extraction, cross-modal information fusion, and highlighting important features. The features of the proposed method include a Transformer-CNN framework for integrated feature extraction, a multi-scale convolutional attention fusion block (MCAFB) for improved detail preservation, and a novel loss function inspired by focal loss for highlighting key areas in the fused image. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that our method performs well on various metrics and significantly improves the fusion quality and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Enhancing Autonomous Navigation: Integration of Artificial Potential Field-Based Reward Functions and Priority Experience Replay
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: In recent years, significant advancements in the field of autonomous navigation for unmanned vehicles have been achieved by applying new deep reinforcement learning methods. However, deep reinforcement learning still faces numerous challenges in autonomous navigation, such as sparse rewards and insufficient utilization of experience. To address above issues, this paper introduces a new algorithm named Artificial Potential field-Enhanced Reinforcement Navigation (APERN). APERN incorporates a reward function design based on the artificial potential field method. This design guides unmanned vehicles to effectively avoid obstacles and reach the target point, addressing the issue of sparse rewards during the exploration process. Concurrently, a priority experience replay mechanism is used in the learning process of the proposed algorithm to sample experiences, which enhances the exploitation of scarce experiences while adjusting priorities to prevent overfitting. Experiments conducted in the Gazebo simulation environment using the APERN algorithm, show that APERN algorithm increases the navigation success rate by approximately 14% over the popular navigation method Goal-Driven Autonomous Exploration (GDAE). Moreover, the model converges more rapidly and exhibits stronger adaptability in complex environments.

articleTitle: Application of Automatic Speech Recognition Theory in Improving Pronunciation and Listening Skills for EFL Learners
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: This paper explores how Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) technology, rooted in human speech recognition research, can be leveraged to enhance English as a Foreign Language learners' pronunciation and listening skills. Inspired by insights gained from ASR, this study introduces a novel theory called the Duality of Pronunciation and a new approach to English pronunciation instruction, known as the Parallel Phonetic Transcription Teaching Method. This approach emphasizes a more holistic understanding of the sound system, focusing on the interconnectedness of sounds within words and phrases. By combining traditional pronunciation drills with advanced techniques and investigating the underlying principles of sound change, this method aims to enhance both pronunciation accuracy and listening comprehension.

articleTitle: Dynamic Graph Contrastive Learning for Neuro Disease Identification using Resting-State fMRI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) techniques provide valuable insights into the connectivity of brain functions during the resting state. Current machine learning and deep learning methodologies have been employed to analyze rs-fMRI data for disease diagnosis; however, these existing approaches necessitate substantial amounts of data. To address this challenge, we propose a Dynamic Graph Contrast Learning (DGCL) framework based on functional MRI for analyzing neurological disorders. The DGCL framework consists of a pre-training phase aimed at generating information-rich fMRI representations using unlabeled training data, followed by a fine-tuning phase dedicated to downstream disease recognition tasks. Specifically, in the pre-training phase, we first apply data augmentation techniques to enhance the fMRI dataset by augmenting blood oxygen level dependent (BOLD) signals. Subsequently, we construct dynamic graphs from the augmented data and utilize two graph encoders for feature extraction from these constructed dynamic graphs through comparative learning. The fine-tuning phase involves training a neural network specifically for disease recognition tasks. Experiments conducted on a rs-fMRI dataset comprising 92 subjects demonstrate that the DGCL framework exhibits strong performance in identifying brain diseases.

articleTitle: Local Context-Aware for Weakly Supervised Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Weakly supervised object detection (WSOD) is designed to learn the class and location information of objects using image-level labels. Traditional WSOD approaches usually utilize Multiple-Instance Learning (MIL) to create numerous proposals and then choose the most distinctive ones as targets. However, methods that rely on convolutional neural networks tend to emphasize the most salient features of an object, often overlooking the complete object boundaries. In this paper, we propose a single-stage Local Context-Aware (LCA) based Transformer for WSOD. We employ category-wide patch mapping (CWPM) to take into account cross-patch information globally. We also incorporate the Local Awakening Module (LAM), which leverages local features to steer the model’s learning process and enhance weak local responses. Comprehensive experiments on the VOC and COCO datasets showcase the efficacy of LCA. Meanwhile, LCA achieves much faster inference speed than the two-stage WSOD approaches.

articleTitle: A Multi-granular Group Decision-Making Approach Integrating Sentiment Analysis for Clustering According to Positivity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Group Decision-Making methods facilitate experts’ collective selection among limited options, which is crucial in improving decisional efficiency. With increasing access to the Internet, both the number of participants and the number of alternatives have increased, diversifying the range of evaluation among experts. Nevertheless, this complexity represents a challenge for traditional Group Decision-Making methods, such as Multi-granular Group Decision-Making, initially designed to handle differences in experts’ decisions as they employ different valuation measures. These methods are now adapted to modern complexities, where experts express their opinions through comments, challenging automated systems that rely on precise languages. Applying Natural Language Processing, especially sentiment analysis, improves the understanding of comments by classifying experts into positive and negative groups. This approach consolidates group evaluations, which are relevant for reaching a consensus and optimising the effectiveness of decisions in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Medical image segmentation is critical for disease detection and therapy, significantly contributing to the enhancement of diagnostic precision and therapeutic efficacy. Given the intrinsic complexity of medical images and the relative scarcity of annotated data, semi-supervised segmentation algorithms demonstrate unique advantages, providing effective solutions for medical image analysis. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the performance of four semi-supervised learning network models in medical image segmentation, including dual-task consistency network (DTC), mutual consistency network (MC-Net), smoothness and class separation network (SS-Net), and bidirectional copy-paste network (BCP), especially focusing on their performance in the case of limited annotated samples. To quantitatively analyze the performance of each model, evaluation metrics such as Dice coefficient, Jaccard coefficient, 95% Hausdorff distance (95HD), and Average Surface Distance (ASD) were employed. The dataset used in the experiment was sourced from the public dataset of the Atrial Segmentation Challenge. The experimental results indicated that MC-Net performed the best across all evaluation metrics, particularly excelling in Dice coefficient and 95HD, demonstrating significant advantages in segmentation accuracy and boundary delineation. BCP exhibited excellent performance in Jaccard coefficient and ASD, while DTC ranked closely to MC-Net in terms of Dice coefficient but slightly lagged in other metrics. SS-Net showed limitations in segmentation accuracy. Confronted with the scarcity of annotated data, this study establishes a theoretical groundwork for improving methodologies in medical image segmentation.

articleTitle: Super-Resolution Reconstruction of UAV Images with GANs: Achievements and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Images taken by UAVs are crucial in many applications due to their ability to provide accurate and thorough information. They are used in various sectors such as agriculture, environmental monitoring, and geology. Although UAVs have advantages, their images may still suffer from issues like blurriness and lower resolution caused by hardware constraints, altitude, and distance. Improving the quality and sharpness of images by using image super-resolution reconstruction is a challenging obstacle in the realm of computer vision, as it requires the transformation of low-resolution images into high-resolution ones. After generative adversarial networks (GANs) were introduced, some models showed promising results in improving image clarity. In this study, we introduce a super resolution GAN (SRGAN) model to improve the resolution of UAV images. By using metrics like Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM), we found that good results in GAN models can be achieved even with a small dataset. The results show an SSIM score of 0.52 and a PSNR score of 30.2 after 8000 epochs. It is recommended to use advanced techniques to enhance SRGAN model performance.

articleTitle: Nighttime Object Detection with Denoising Diffusion-Probabilistic Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Object detection is essential for road safety, aiding drivers in identifying vehicles, pedestrians, and other road objects. However, nighttime detection remains challenging due to low visibility impacting the accuracy of current object detection models. This paper proposes a novel approach that uses a denoising diffusion-probabilistic model to enhance nighttime object detection performance. It is trained for conditional image translation, converting nighttime images into daytime images through a forward process that adds Gaussian noise. The reverse process predicts and removes the added noise to reconstruct the daytime image. Experimental results indicate that this method significantly improves vehicle detection accuracy at night compared to state-of-the-art detectors.

articleTitle: SUM-GAN-FGN: Frequency Domain Unsupervised Video Summarization with Gaussian Noise Based on GAN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Video summarization focuses on extracting a concise set of frames from the original video that retains the most information possible. Most of the current mainstream technologies for video summarization start from the perspective of time domain, framing summarization as a recurrent neural network (RNN) sequence prediction challenge. However, time domain modeling is difficult to use the spatial position information and sound information in the video. In this work, we analyze this problem from a frequency domain perspective. By leveraging the fast Fourier transform (FFT), we extract spectral features and then input it into the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to reconstruct the video in an unsupervised manner and then generate a summary. Furthermore, the predicted values for frame importance scores are approximately uniformly distributed, leading to the problem of ineffective feature learning. We add Gaussian noise (auxiliary signal) to frame importance scores to improve keyframe classification accuracy. Considering the subjectivity of labeling for video summarization tasks, we output multiple sets of means and variances of frame importance scores, and use a small, linear neural network layer to learn the best-fit set to improve label confidence. Our experiments on two benchmark datasets (SumMe and TVSum) indicated the competitiveness of our approach. Especially on the former dataset, our F-Score score is as high as 54.5%, achieving excellent performance at present.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for License Plate Number Recognition: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: With the continuous development of deep learning technology, object detection has become an important research direction in this field. The purpose of this study is to review the deep learning techniques and typical deep networks for license plate number detection and recognition in recent years, including CNN, RNN, GAN, Transformer, and Diffusion Model. Furthermore, we compare the advantages and disadvantages of these methods. Finally, some challenges and future development directions of deep learning technology in license plate number detection and recognition are pointed out.

articleTitle: Research on the development and application of high-precision 5G timing Terminal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Since the official issuance of 5G licenses in China, 5G networks have begun to be deployed and promoted in an orderly way. At present, the domestic 5G network has a foundation for widespread application. Power grid is an industry closely related to information and communication technology, 5G is bound to bring changes to the existing power network. Especially in the distribution grid, a large number of sensors and protection devices are scattered in the grid, so it is necessary to develop a 5G communication terminal with low cost, easy to use and high precision timing ability. By analyzing the time synchronization architecture of 5G network, this paper introduces a 5G communication timing terminal that can use 5G network to output IRIG-B (Inter-range Instrumentation Group-B format) code. The paper introduces its implementation principle and typical application scenarios in detail, which provides reference for the combination of power grid and 5G technology.

articleTitle: Psychological Intrusion Detection System: Securing Cyber-Physical Systems Through Urgency Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Due to the growing reliance on technology in society, cyber-physical systems have gained popularity in various fields: industrial control systems, communications networks, and more. Nevertheless, cyber-attacks have increased, especially on the data transmission layer used for routing and communication. Previous literature has demonstrated the promise of using machine learning in network intrusion detection. However, the effectiveness of urgency cues has not been investigated for this task. Urgency is defined by the psychological tendency to complete tasks within a certain time frame based on emotional motives. Thus, the researcher proposes a novel, machine learning algorithm to detect network intrusion based on added urgency metrics. Specifically, positive urgency cues, created by positive emotions and success, and negative urgency cues, formed from negative emotions and failures, are used to represent attacker behavior, which are then incorporated into a machine learning model for intrusion detection. The concept of successes and failures is associated with an attacker’s achievement of elevated permissions, commands executed, and more. These tasks are considered within a time frame to compute an attacker’s positive and negative urgency. These urgency levels are represented in various manners (binary coding, categorical representation, numerical level) to determine the best representation of urgency in intrusion detection. Through various machine learning models, the researcher observed the highest accuracy of 98.91% with a random forest classifier and improvements of up to 11.18% in accuracy for all models using the additional urgency metrics. Thus, the researcher constructed a reliable intrusion detection model that applies the psychological theory of urgency.

articleTitle: Lip-reading: Phoneme-to-text Machine Translation using Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: An effective conversion of recognised phonemes to words has a significant impact on the overall performance of an automatic lip-reading system. In this paper, transformer-based models have been examined for phoneme-to-text translation. The benchmark BBC Lip-reading Sentence 2 (LRS2) data is used in this study, and the T5 model (Text-To-Text Transfer Transformer) and the GPT-2 model are considered the conversion models. A detailed discussion is provided on the analysis procedure, data pre-processing, model implementation, and the metrics employed for model evaluation. The experimental results have demonstrated that the T5 model can achieve a substantial improvement over the GPT-2 model with a superior accuracy and fluency in the phoneme-to-text translation, offering a potentially promising solution for enhancing the precision of automatic translation and speech processing systems. This work contributes to the development of more robust applications in the field of speech recognition and communication technologies.

articleTitle: Underwater target encirclement by multi-UUV based on finite-time event-triggered time-varying formation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: This paper studies underwater target encirclement control for underactuated Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUVs), with a focus on improving system convergence speed, overcoming the disturbance of ocean currents and limitations of underwater target velocity measurement, and conserving resources. Firstly, to avoid the degradation of control performance due to inaccurate target velocity measurement, a finite-time observer is designed based on the target’s position to estimate the target’s velocity. Secondly, a velocity error observer is designed to observe the velocity error between the UUVs and the target. Finally, a finite-time controller is designed based on the event-triggered mechanism to ensure that multiple UUVs encircle the target in a time-varying formation within a finite time without the need for global information of the system. The non-existence of Zeno behavior in the system is mathematically proven, and the effectiveness of the method is validated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Exploring the Crowdsourced Emergency Information Collaborative Management Model Using Constructing Grounded Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: This study investigates the collaborative and cooperative relationships among participants in different tasks within crowdsourced emergency information management practices during emergencies. Summarizing the theoretical model of crowdsourced emergency information collaborative management can enhance the overall effectiveness of emergency information management. Using the Constructing Grounded Theory method, this study codes, analyzes, and summarizes qualitative materials from two specific cases during the Henan 7.20 rainstorm event: the "Lifesaving Document" and the "Rescue Information Map." This process aims to identify the basic structure and operating mechanisms of the crowdsourced emergency information collaborative management model. The results indicate that the crowdsourced emergency information collaborative management model operates in the unique management environment of emergencies, involving the collaborative participation of emergency information providers, processors, disseminators, and users. Through crowdsourcing tasks that connect emergency information flows across data, behavior, and system layers, the goal of collaborative management of emergency information is achieved.

articleTitle: A Survey of Industrial Surface Defect Detection Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Surface defect detection in industrial production is crucial. Traditional image processing techniques face limitations when dealing with complex textures, background noise, and lighting variations. As deep learning technology advances, its applications across various fields have become increasingly widespread, displaying notable benefits in terms of performance in real time and great precision. the utilization of deep learning for the detection of surface defects in industrial settings. According to the metal surface, texture surface and other surfaces of industrial surface defect detection, three aspects of defect segmentation, defect detection and defect classification are studied in detail. By analyzing and comparing different methods, we explore the practical effects of deep learning technology in various industrial surface defect detections, highlighting current challenges and potential future directions.

articleTitle: Attention Methods for Image Denoising: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Image denoising is an important branch of image processing, which is developed from traditional mechina learning methods to deep learning methods. Over the past few years, the focus on attention mechanisms has grown, owing to their substantial impact on various image processing applications. After the Transformer architecture was proposed, more attention mechanism-based research and improvements were proposed. However, there are few researches on image denoising based on different attention techniques. Hence, this paper delivers an exhaustive examination and overview of the utilization of attention mechanisms for image noise reduction over the past few years. We have presented three prevalent attention strategies: spatial attention, channel attention, and self-attention, and evaluated the efficacy of attention-driven image denoising techniques. Finally, this paper discusses the problems and challenges in current research and provides some inspiration for future research directions.

articleTitle: Research on manned/unmanned aircraft formation cooperative task allocation based on hierarchical hybrid auction algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The manned/unmanned aircraft collaborative task allocation is developed on the basis of the multi-UAV task planning method, which can give full play to the pilot's human intelligence at critical moments, and is a complement to the lower intelligence of UAVs to improve the system's environmental adaptability and effectiveness. In this paper, we propose a task allocation method based on hierarchical decision-making mechanism and contract net auction algorithm improvement. From the perspective of confrontation between two sides of the air war, the types of tasks that UAVs need to perform in the battlefield are analysed. In the process of task bundle construction, each attribute value of the tasks in the battlefield is quantified, and then handed over to the manned aircraft decision-making mechanism to construct a reasonable auction sequence. In the auction process, target coverage and penalty terms are introduced to improve the objective function, which is used to balance the task allocation load among UAVs. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by experimental simulation.

articleTitle: A Benchmark Conservation Relevance Inference Method for Explaining Deep Networks with Multiple Feature Extraction Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the counterfactual inference methods will cause relevance drift when interpreting the deep networks with multiple feature extraction structures, which leads to inaccurate interpretation, this paper proposes a benchmark conservation relevance inference method based on direct contribution (BCRI). By ensuring the consistency of the relevance propagation of multiple feature extraction structures, BCRI can overcome the relevance drift, and can accurately and quickly analyze the relevance of each input variable. This method can carry out the reasonable analysis of the model and understand the model behavior pattern. Experimental results show that the proposed method can generate more trustworthy counterfactual interpretations efficiently than other methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing Functional Brain Network Construction for Neurological Disorder Diagnosis through Modularity-Driven Regularization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The burgeoning field of Functional Brain Network (FBN) analysis has emerged as a promising avenue for diagnosing neurological disorders. As innovative biomarkers, FBNs offer a novel perspective on probing the intricacies of brain connectivity. However, the fidelity of FBN construction depends on the quality of data acquisition, which is often a formidable challenge due to inherent limitations. Inspired by the no free lunch theorem, a straightforward ambition is to integrate the exogenous knowledge to enhance the fidelity of FBNs. Motivated by this ambition, this paper provides a Modularity-Driven Regularization (MDR) for the FBN construction. Specifically, we design and incorporate a dyadic L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> regulariser into the FBN model to formulate the modularity prior. Furthermore, we have developed a generalized alternating multiplier method algorithm for the estimation of the FBN. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our MDR, we perform rigorous experiments on a Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) identification task using the NITRC dataset. The validity of our model has been confirmed by the experimental outcomes. Additionally, it enhances biomarker precision for diagnosing neurological disorders like MCI, supporting potential early intervention strategies.

articleTitle: Research on Hybrid Collaborative Filtering Hotel Recommendation Algorithm Based on Online Reviews and Ratings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: In addressing the challenges of information overload and the filter bubble in online hotel reservations, this paper proposes a hybrid collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm that leverages online hotel reviews, likes, and rating data. Firstly, the algorithm utilizes the advantage of probabilistic linguistic term sets to handle fuzzy semantics, aggregating and expressing hotel feature information from online reviews. This information is further refined by adjusting with the number of likes on the reviews. Then, the maximum deviation method is employed to determine the weights of the hotel attributes. By combining cosine similarity and adjusted cosine similarity to integrate pessimistic and optimistic results, a fused similarity measure is obtained. Hotel rating similarities are calculated based on user ratings. The hybrid similarity is derived by obtaining a weighted sum of the fused similarity and rating similarity. Subsequently, this hybrid similarity is employed to construct the hybrid similarity matrix. Finally, the recommendation results are generated, incorporating user historical data. An empirical analysis was conducted using ten hotels in Shenzhen to validate the effectiveness of the hybrid algorithm. The findings demonstrate that the proposed algorithm enriches the research on hotel recommendation systems to some extent.

articleTitle: Improved Domain-Adversarial Neural Networks with Mixup and Pseudo-Labeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Domain adaptation is essential for transferring knowledge from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain, a process especially critical in healthcare due to the high costs and challenges associated with data collection and annotation. Domain-Adversarial Neural Networks (DANN) use adversarial training to reduce the feature distribution differences between the source and target domains. However, DANN primarily focuses on aligning feature distributions, potentially overlooking the valuable intrinsic characteristics present within the target domain. To overcome these challenges, we introduce an improved DANN framework that incorporates mixup and pseudo-labeling techniques. Mixup, a data augmentation method, generates new training samples by linearly interpolating between pairs of examples, enhancing the model’s generalization capability. Pseudo-labeling, a semi-supervised learning strategy, assigns labels to unlabeled data based on the model’s predictions. By integrating these techniques, our framework effectively leverages target domain data, improving domain adaptation performance. Experimental results indicate that our method surpasses conventional DANN approaches across multiple benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Design of Road Traffic Management and Control Network Architecture Based on SDN: An Innovative Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The design of a road management and control network architecture based on SDN (Software Defined Network) is of great significance. The SDN architecture separates the control plane from the data plane, bringing a new perspective and methods to road traffic management. In order to integrate the “programmability” concept of SDN into traffic management, this paper proposes a road traffic management and control network architecture based on SDN, which consists of the operation layer, control layer, and application layer, to achieve centralized management and scheduling of traffic flow and traffic management equipment within the road network. The paper focuses on the introduction of the core centralized controller of the SDN architecture, discussing the design from the perspectives of the southbound interface, northbound interface, hierarchical architecture of the controller, and software platform. The proposed Software Defined Traffic Management (SDTM) network architecture has the distinct advantages of digitalization of traffic elements, centralized traffic control, and open programmability of the system, playing a crucial role in solving traffic congestion and improving traffic safety, and promoting the level of road traffic management to a new level.

articleTitle: Development of a refined wave field forecast model based on LSTM and its application in the Qiongzhou Strait
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: This paper develops a refined wave field prediction model based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Enhancements in the dataset and feature selection are implemented to improve predictive performance. The dataset is derived from a self-moored buoy in the Qiongzhou Strait. The ERA5 reanalysis dataset is used for validation of the buoy's measurements. To enhance the model’s prediction efficiency, additional models are built using Random Forest and XGBoost, where the feature importance for time steps t-3, t-6, and t-12, relative to the current time (t), is ranked for predicting average wave height. Comparative models based on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) are also constructed for wave height prediction. The evaluation criteria— Mean Square Error (MSE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and the Coefficient of Determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)—confirm that the proposed model outperforms other comparison models, achieving the best results when predicting the next hour's average wave height using data from the previous three hours.

articleTitle: Topology-Enhanced Multi-Modal Residual Graph Convolutional Network for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Functional Brain Networks (FBNs) have shown promise in diagnosing neurological disorders, particularly Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Currently, Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) excel in processing FBN data, making them instrumental in learning from functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) and analyzing ASD. Despite their advantages, existing methods primarily concentrate on the structural properties of brain networks, often overlooking the essential topological information. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Topologically Enhanced Multi-Pattern Residual Graph Learning (TEMPRGL) framework. Our approach begins by constructing diverse brain networks from fMRI data, capturing a range of connectivity patterns. We then employ a dual-feature extraction strategy on FBNs: one that utilizes multiple Residual GCN modules to generate multi-modal graph representations, which are subsequently integrated; and another focuses on combining topology information from FBN. To validate our TEMPRGL, we exeperiment on the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) dataset. It attained an impressively high accuracy rate of 92.5%., underscoring its effectiveness in neurological disorder diagnosis.

articleTitle: SceNDD++: An Enhanced Scenario-based Naturalistic Driving Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: This paper presents SceNDD++, a novel scenariobased naturalistic driving dataset and an enhanced version of the previously published SceNDD dataset. Naturalistic driving data collected in different regions in the USA, including Austin, San Diego, Washington DC, and Indianapolis was included in the new dataset. The dataset encapsulates a wide array of real driving scenarios with heterogeneous trajectories and behaviors. It comprises data from both the ego vehicle and non-ego actors, incorporating elements such as waypoints, velocity, yaw angle, and dimensions of the bounding boxes. The dataset allows users to incorporate additional actors, sensors, roads, and obstacles. Compared to its predecessor SceNDD, SceNDD++ is more robust by integrating different vulnerable road users (VRUs), such as pedestrians and bicyclists, and featuring smoother trajectories of non-ego actors.

articleTitle: Adaptive Optimization Multi-Layer Perceptron for Emotion Recognition from EEG Brain Maps
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Emotion recognition is an important issue in Affective Computing and Human Computer Interaction, and plays a crucial role in interpersonal communication and media effectiveness. In recent years, there has been a surge of interest in the field of emotion recognition, driven by advancements in machine learning models and computer vision techniques. These technologies have the potential to revolutionize the way people understand and interpret human emotions. This paper proposes a new electroencephalography (EEG) emotion recognition dataset based on daily media content that serves as emotion-inducing materials, including 16 video clips, 65 valid EEG signals and valence-arousal states self-assessment reports of subjects. And a novel EEG emotion recognition model based on multi-layer perceptron taking brain maps as spatial representations is proposed, using genetic algorithm to adaptively optimize the multi-layer perceptron structure in the algorithm that uses brain maps as input data and aims to predict emotional states of valence and arousal.
