The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper has better performance than existing results in the literature.

articleTitle: Monarch Butterfly Optimization Algorithm for Human-Robot Collaboration Multi-Objective Disassembly Line Balancing Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Efficient end-of-life products disassembly is crucial in the remanufacturing process. However, hazardous and repetitive disassembly tasks raise labor costs and decrease safety and efficiency. This work proposes an innovative disassembly algorithm that is inspired by monarch butterfly, aiming at improving disassembly efficiency through the utilization of human-robot collaboration in the context of a hybrid disassembly line for repetitive or hazardous tasks. The model in this paper provides the basis of solving the multi-objective problem and the mixed integer programming problem. The purpose is to improve the profit in the human robot cooperation environment, and reduce the standby time of the workstation as much as possible. Comparison of this algorithm with other intelligent optimization algorithms with experiments shows its competitive performance in both profit and idle time.

articleTitle: Towards Intelligent and Trustworthy Crowdsourcing Systems with Cyber-physical Social Intelligence via Retrieval-augmented Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: In recent years, crowdsourcing systems that tackle complex tasks through the collective efforts of many individuals have garnered substantial attention. However, the existing crowd-sourcing systems face some challenges such as overreliance on human experience and effort, information overload, and risks of privacy breaches. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes an intelligent and trustworthy crowdsourcing frame-work based on blockchain and retrieval-augmented generation. The framework centers around foundational models to integrate the three distinct and sequentially interdependent phases: task decomposition, task allocation or recommendation, and task execution, enabling the automatic provision of a personalized, comfortable, and efficient user experience. Blockchain and smart contracts are utilized to protect user privacy and interests without leaning on any third trusted authority. Additionally, the operational process of the framework is explained and validated by taking printed circuit board design and manufacturing as a case study and ChatGPT as its generator.

articleTitle: Enhancing Efficiency of Automated Medication Delivery via Reinforcement Learning in Hospital Settings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: With the rapid advances in robotics and automation science, robots have been taking over more and more jobs that used to be performed by humans. Automated medication delivery with robots can free up nurses from the workload. Path planning for robots is a hot research topic, which is particularly important in hospital settings. In this paper, we propose to use a reinforcement learning approach to find optimal medication delivery paths. The optimization objective is to minimize the time span for delivering medications to all patient rooms. Practical factors such as collision avoidance are considered. To reduce the action space of the reinforcement learning agent, unreasonable actions are filtered to save the training time.

articleTitle: MCMS-Net: an underwater target detection network based on Multi-Conv Multi-Scale feature fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Influenced by the complex characteristics of the marine environment, a Multi-Conv Multi-Scale Network (MCMS-Net), a multi-scale feature fusion network for underwater target detection, is proposed to address the problem of poor underwater target detection accuracy due to the difficulty of capturing target features of marine organisms. Firstly, a backbone network MCM Backbone stacked by Multi-Conv Module1 (MCM1) and Multi-Conv Module2 (MCM2) is designed to improve the amount of feature residual information of the target to be detected in the network, which is conducive to the subsequent feature transfer. Secondly, the SE attention mechanism is introduced to improve the network’s ability to capture shallow and high-level feature information through the MCM2-Path Aggregation Network (MCM2-PANet) with multi-scale feature fusion. Finally, an anchor frame-based MCM Detection Head is designed to improve the detection accuracy of different targets by combining multiple sets of convolutional module operations with different sized feature layers. Experiments show that the algorithm is able to reach 82.8% detection accuracy on underwater target URPC dataset, which is informative for target detection applications of underwater robots in real engineering.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Multitask Learning Model for Chinese Grammatical Error Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Grammatical error detection is important in natural language processing and has developed rapidly in recent years. Most existing studies based on neural networks have achieved good performances. However, similar to other studies pertaining to natural language processing, such as part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition, severe data imbalance is encountered: the number of negative samples is significantly greater than the number of positive samples. This results in the tendency of learning negative samples during model training. Hence, we define the Chinese grammatical error detection problem as a hierarchical task and propose a hierarchical multitask learning model. The first and second levels comprise grammatical error detection and error type classification tasks, respectively. In the former task, the model only detects grammatical errors and does not distinguish error types, and it is known as a coarse-grained network. In the latter task, the model classifies the detected grammatical errors into their corresponding categories, and it is known as a fine-grained network. By doing this, the positive class information in the first-level task can be increased, and the accuracy of the second-level task further improved. Therefore, we cast each level as a subtask and developed a multitask learning framework based on the two subtasks. Experimental results show that the performance of the proposed method is better than that of the basic model, particularly in term of position level.

articleTitle: Enhancing Image Clustering with CLIP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Both similarity of instances and difference among clusters play an essential role in improving the performance of deep image clustering. Existing deep clustering methods often fail to capture both consistency and distinctness of semantics when the label information is not available. In this work, we propose a semantic prototype pseudo-label-based image clustering model, which uses a CLIP image encoder as the feature model and incorporates an ensemble-based clustering head. The feature model is responsible for evaluating the consistency between instances, while the clustering prediction head is used to discern semantic differences. The prototype pseudo-label algorithm is designed to train the clustering head to effectively improve the accuracy and reliability of self-supervision. The optimization of the clustering network is divided into two stages, both of which do not rely on real labels: 1) The feature model is trained using contrastive loss to evaluate the consistency of instances; 2) The clustering head is trained using the prototype pseudo-label algorithm to distinguish between semantic categories. Comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in improving clustering performance, especially achieving a 10% improvement on three recognized evaluation metrics compared to existing techniques on the STL-10 and ImageNet-10 datasets.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Variable Window Attention Network for Continuous Sign Language Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Sign language is primarily conveyed through hands and face movements. Therefore, a pivotal challenge in continuous sign language recognition (CSLR) is the meticulous modeling and interpreting of visual cues emanating from hands and facial movements. However, contemporary CSLR methods have exhibited limitations in adequately capturing information from both the hands and facial regions, often overlooking the continuity, and correlations across multiple consecutive frames. To mitigate these shortcomings, we propose the Multi-scale Variable Window Attention Network (MVAN). This framework fuses the strengths of an improved Efficient Multi-scale Attention (iEMA) with Variable Window Adaptation (VWA) attention. Specifically, iEMA first scans information spatially at multiple scales to simultaneously capture information from areas such as hands and faces, and models spatial continuity interactions between them, enhancing spatial features. Secondly, VWA dynamically changes its window size at the temporal level to adaptively capture complex temporal changes in hands and face movements in successive frames. Thus, VWA can effectively model the continuity and correlation between hands and face movements to have the ability to capture sign language movements of different lengths. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that our proposed MVAN strengthens the visual feature extraction of hands and face, improving the recognition performance.

articleTitle: Generalizable Gaze Synthesis for Practical Fatigue Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Fatigue has been established as a significant factor affecting both productivity and safety across a range of industries. Traditional self-reporting methods are commonly used for fatigue detection, but they are inherently subjective and lack real-time monitoring capabilities. Although objective methods, such as electroencephalograms and facial features, have proven to be reliable and effective in detecting fatigue, their susceptibility to noisy environments and privacy concerns significantly constrain their practical applications. To address these issues, this paper proposes the VisioPhysio Fatigue Detector (VPFD) as a practical solution to fatigue management. By utilizing two commercially-available wearable devices: HoloLens 2 and Google Pixel Watch 2, VPFD integrates visual and physiological signals to detect fatigue in a non-intrusive. Given the limited publicly available datasets for fatigue and unique strengths of the modalities used in these datasets, the paper introduces an innovative data synthesis method that has been experimentally proven to be effective.

articleTitle: Designing Games for Cognitive and Emotional Integration in Mathematics Education: Insights from Teacher Interviews and Game Design Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The research investigates cognitive-motivational imbalances in game-based interventions targeting children’s math anxiety. Study 1: Utilizing grounded theory, interviews were conducted with six primary school mathematics teachers, leading to the development of a cognitive-emotional support model for mathematics learning. Study 2: Analysis of review data from 68 mathematics games revealed that the design of these games needs to integrate multiple aspects, including body, cognitive, emotional, and psychological considerations.

articleTitle: Self-supervised Outlier Segmentation-guided Face De-occlusion Using 3D Facial Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Occlusion is a common occurrence in facial images and videos captured in the wild. Effective face de-occlusion is of paramount importance for enhancing the robustness of user identity verification and security systems. To this end, we propose a novel self-supervised GAN-based framework for face de-occlusion in this study, which integrates 3D facial reconstruction with outlier segmentation guidance, termed as 3DOG-GAN. In 3DOG-GAN, we introduce an outlier segmentation module that utilizes statistical priors to generate accurate occlusion masks, facilitating the de-occlusion process. Furthermore, we design a GAN-based dual-branch module, which is capable of simultaneously generating the occlusion mask and the de-occluded face. Extensive experiments on the widely-used datasets demonstrate the superior performance of 3DOG-GAN on existing methods.

articleTitle: E-TD3: A Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Autonomous Flight Decision-Making Method for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: As the application of unmanned aerial vehicles(UAVs) in low-altitude airspace continues to broaden, higher requirements have been placed on their autonomous and intelligent manoeuvring and adaptive capabilities. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes an end-to-end UAV flight decision-making method based on deep reinforcement learning, and provides a dynamic planning scheme for the mission of safely and stably avoiding the threat of environmental obstacles and tracking the target. The method is based on the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) framework and introduces the Gated Recurrent Unit. To further improve the exploration capability and sample efficiency of the algorithm, we integrate expert experience into reinforcement learning and thus propose the E-TD3 algorithm. We reconstructed the experience replay buffer and designed a mixed sample collection mechanism to dynamically adjust the proportion of demonstration data. Finally, we perform experimental validation on the AirSim platform.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Stains Reduction with Diffusion Models for Ancient Japanese Manuscripts
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Ancient Japanese manuscripts are a valuable cultural heritage that allows us to understand the culture and values of the past. However, due to preservation over hundreds of years, stains result in antique manuscripts, and they cause low readability and loss of contents to the manuscripts. Considering preserving these assets through virtual restoration, we propose a two-stage stain reduction based on Denoising Diffusion Restoration Models (DDRM). The stain reduction proceeds by combining removing background by the binarization and reconstruction of before-processing images by DDRM. In addition, the sequential conducting that contains patches of book pages and entire them leads to preserving local information and ensuring consistency across the pages. Generation results are qualitatively improved and more realistic than traditional binarization. Also, the proposal method is evaluated by two aspects, the stain reduction metrics and preserving characters metrics. The evaluation result shows our proposal is more effective and achieves higher restoration quality than conventional binarization.

articleTitle: Universum Inspired Graph Contrast Learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The functional brain network (FBN) has recently emerged as a pivotal biomarker in the diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Meanwhile, graph convolutional networks (GCNs) represent a promising strategy for the concurrent extraction of FBN features and the facilitation of ASD identification. Unfortunately, the efficacy of existing GCN methods is often limited by their reliance on extensive annotated datasets. To address this limitation, we propose the Universum Inspired Graph Contrast Learning (Uni-GCL) framework, a novel approach to brain disease analysis that capitalizes on the generation of Universum samples for the pre-training of the GCN model. Specifically, we use a Mixup technique to generate universum samples and design a universum-inspired contrastive loss function. This methodology necessitates only a modest number of samples for finetuning the pre-trained model, effectively reducing data requirements while simultaneously boosting model performance. To systematically assess the performance of Uni-GCL, we conducted rigorous experiments on the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) initiative for ASD identification. The results demonstrate that Uni-GCL, augmented with universum samples, yields compelling outcomes, underscoring its potential as a robust method in the diagnostic arsenal for ASD.

articleTitle: Microscope Autofocus Based on Difference of Gaussians and Triplet Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Whole slide imaging (WSI) involves scanning tissue specimens on slides using a microscope and converting them into digital formats, thereby preserving comprehensive tissue information to assist clinical diagnosis. High-precision autofocus methods are crucial for ensuring the quality of WSI. However, existing autofocus methods can be affected by variations in staining methods and sample differences. This paper introduces a robust autofocus method based on Difference of Gaussians (DoG) image and triplet loss. By utilizing DoG image to emphasize image edge information that is highly correlated with focus distance, this method helps reduce the impact of staining variations. Furthermore, triplet loss enhances the network model’s sensitivity to defocus distance, effectively addressing the issue of sample shape differences. Comparative and ablation experiments conducted on publicly available datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: Synthesizing Aβ-PET based on multi-modal neuroimaging fusion for pathological diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: Synthesizing Aβ-PET images from cross-modal neuroimaging for diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease through multi-modal medical image fusion is highly significant. However, there are relatively few studies in this area. We propose a multi-modal fusion adversarial method for Aβ-PET medical image synthesis, named MultiMed, to generate Aβ-PET images by fusing features from T1 and Flair images. Our approach employs an end-to-end method for image generation, incorporating a Multi-Feature Fusion Stream module for feature fusion. Integrating multimodal features enhances the model’s representation capability and preliminarily designed a visual domain classifier for Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis. We constructed an internal dataset for model training and validated our model on two external validation sets, achieving notable performance.

articleTitle: Research on Hybrid Hotel Recommendation Algorithm Based on Probabilistic Linguistic Term Sets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: This paper takes hotels as a typical tourism product and addresses the personalized and accurate recommendation needs and cold start problems in hotel recommendations. It introduces a hybrid hotel recommendation algorithm that incorporates probabilistic language term sets and online reviews, functioning as a switching-type hybrid approach. For returning users, an improved collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm is used, which fully integrates the advantages of probabilistic language term sets in processing fuzzy semantics. Firstly, the algorithm is based on the extraction and expression of the featuress of the hotel, and then the maximum deviation method is applied to determine the weights of the hotel properties. Lastly, it calculates the fused similarity matrix for hotels, combining adjusted cosine similarity with user ratings. The recommendation results are generated by combining the user's historical data. For new users, a user preference-based recommendation algorithm is used, which fully utilizes the online review text data of returning users and the historical search data of new users. The algorithm first collects and expresses hotel feature information from online reviews using probabilistic language term sets, constructs a hotel evaluation matrix, and then builds a user preference matrix derived from the user's past interaction data. The similarity matrix is calculated by cosinesimilarity, and the hotel is recommended based on similarity and hotel recommendations are provided according to the resulting similarity scores. This study performs a case analysis involving ten hotels in Macau, China, to assess the performance of the proposed hybrid algorithm. Different recommendation strategies are adopted for different users to meet their needs. This algorithm enriches the research on hotel recommendation algorithms to some extent.

articleTitle: Incremental Image Captioning with Attention to Transient via Kolmogorov-Arnold Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: In this work, we present an incremental learning framework for image captioning, enabling models to learn new tasks across various image domains. We introduce the integration of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) with attention-enhanced long short-term memory (LSTM), mapping output features to vocabulary probability distributions for next-word prediction, termed "RATT-KAN". The encoder employs a contrastive continual learning loss for flexible adaptation to new tasks. Furthermore, within the decoder, under the task-specific Recurrent Attention to Transient Tasks (RATT) attention parameters, we incorporate the KAN to replace the traditional linear classifier. By utilizing the β-spline function provides greater flexibility and stability, thereby mitigating forgetting. We evaluated the image captioning task on the Microsoft Common Objects in Context (MS-COCO) and Flickr30K datasets. The experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of our newly developed comprehensive model.

articleTitle: Multi-View Comparative Self-Supervised Graph Learning for Neuro-disease Diagnosis Using Functional Brain Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Cyber-Physical Social Intelligence (ICCSI)
abstract: The burgeoning interest in diagnosing neurological diseases through the analysis of functional brain networks (FBNs) has been a focal point of recent research. Despite the promise of this approach, conventional graph learning techniques are often constrained by their reliance on extensive datasets annotated with clinical information. To transcend this constraint, we introduce a novel self-supervised graph learning model, termed Multi-View Comparative Self-Supervised Graph Learning (MCS-GL), which leverages Personalized PageRank (PPR) to increase samples and uses local-global information as multi view for comparative learning to enhance FBN-based diagnostics. With this approach, a pre-trained model is designed to generate information-rich Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging(fMRI) representations from unlabeled training data. Fine-tuning the model for downstream disease identification tasks significantly reduces the requirement for large amounts of labeled training data. We have rigorously evaluated the efficacy of our MCS-GL model through its application to an autism diagnosis task. The experimental outcomes not only substantiate the superiority of our model but also underscore the pivotal role of self-supervised learning in advancing FBN-based diagnostics of neurological diseases.
